mods.description: Mod compatible everything — blocks, tools, You Name It! Every survival-obtainable block in the game, vanilla or modded, gets its own full tool and armour set, generated and textured at load time.

releases.notes:
**Fixes the crash properly, including on worlds you have already played.**

1.0.2 stopped new items being given an id the game reads as a block, but an allocator only governs what it hands out next — ids already written into an existing world do not move because the mod was updated. Those saved items could still bring the game down whenever a pig or sheep was nearby, with no interaction needed. The lookup itself is now guarded, so a stack the game cannot resolve is simply ignored.

If you were crashing on 1.0.2, this is the one you want.

**Requires** Better than Adventure! `8.0.1` and [HalpLibe](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-halplibe) `6.1.0`+. Keeping [Useless Numerical](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-useless-numerical) installed is still recommended, so saved gear is matched by name.

Download `younameit-BTA8.0.X-obf.jar` and drop it in your instance's `.minecraft/mods/` folder.

releases.notes:
Fixes a crash. Generated items could be given an id inside the block range, and the game reads that range as blocks in a few places — so holding one near a pig or a sheep, or middle-clicking it, could bring the game down. Ids are now kept out of that range entirely, and more sets fit than before.

**Updating an existing world:** generated items change id in this version. Keep [Useless Numerical](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-useless-numerical) installed so saved gear is matched by name rather than by number.

Wooden, stone, iron, gold and diamond armour became craftable in 1.0.1 and are included here.

**Requires** Better than Adventure! `8.0.1` and [HalpLibe](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-halplibe) `6.1.0`+.

Download `younameit-BTA8.0.X-obf.jar` and drop it in your instance's `.minecraft/mods/` folder.

releases.notes:
## Built for Better than Adventure! `8.0.1` (release channel)

First public release of **You Name It!** — every block in the game becomes a full tool and armour
set: pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, sword, helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots.

Nothing is hand-listed. The mod walks the block and item registries as the game loads and generates
a set for everything it finds, so blocks added by **other mods get sets too**, with no patch and no
compatibility list. On a vanilla 8.0.1 install that's **810 sets — 7,290 items — in about 180 ms**
at startup.

Textures aren't recolours of one template. The mod diffs two of BTA's *own* sprites for the same
tool in different materials, keeps the pixels that are identical between them (the wooden handle,
the outline, the specular highlight) and repaints the pixels that differ. Per-tool shapes come out
right for free, and a resource pack that redraws the vanilla tools is followed rather than fought.

### Download

**[`younameit-1.0.0-BTA8.0.1-obf.jar`](https://github.com/colinthepwner/younameit-bta/releases/download/v1.0.0/younameit-1.0.0-BTA8.0.1-obf.jar)**
— drop it in your instance's `.minecraft/mods/` folder, alongside HalpLibe.

### Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| **Better than Adventure!** | **`8.0.1`** |
| Mod loader | Babric / Fabric loader `0.18.4-bta.11`+ |
| [HalpLibe](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-halplibe) | `6.1.0`+ — **required**, install it alongside |
| Java | 17+ |
| [ModMenu](https://github.com/Turnip-Labs/bta-modmenu) | optional, for in-game config |

HalpLibe is **not** bundled inside the jar, so it won't shadow a newer copy you already have.

### Notes

- The jar is ProGuard-renamed. It's a renamer only — no shrinking, no optimising — and the
  entrypoint classes plus the whole mixin package are left readable on purpose, because the loader
  and Mixin resolve those by name.
- Config is written to `config/younameit.properties` on first launch. Everything is switchable
  there: tools, armour, recipes, the fire set bonus, id ranges, and the speed bonus a tool gets on
  its own block.
- Item ids are allocated automatically and will relocate if the configured base range is already
  occupied, so it should behave in a busy modpack.
